category: Physics interfaces II: electromagnetics, acoustics, chemical & multiphysics
description: The wave, field and transport side of the COMSOL Model Builder: the AC/DC, RF and Wave Optics electromagnetic interfaces and their ports, terminals and absorbing conditions; pressure and thermoviscous acoustics; species transport, reaction engineering and electrochemistry; the general-purpose Mathematics PDE and ODE interfaces; and the Multiphysics coupling nodes that join two interfaces into one solved system. Each entry gives the Add Physics or right-click path plus COMSOL API for Java calls, where the last integer in create() is the entity dimension (3 = domain in 3D, 2 = boundary in 3D, 1 = edge, 0 = point).

tools.name: Electrostatics (es)
tools.description: Solves Gauss's law in potential form, -div(epsilon0*epsilon_r*grad(V)) = rho_v, for the electric potential V, plus the derived field E = -grad(V) and displacement D. Supports stationary, time-dependent (quasi-static), frequency-domain (for lossy dielectrics) and small-signal studies in 3D, 2D, 2D axisymmetric and 1D. Use it for capacitors, MEMS actuators, insulators, high-voltage bushings, dielectrophoresis, capacitive sensors and any problem where no significant current flows; use Electric Currents (ec) instead when conduction matters.
tools.usage: Model Wizard / Add Physics > AC/DC > Electric Fields and Currents > Electrostatics (es)

parameters.name: Relative permittivity epsilon_r
parameters.description: Set on the Charge Conservation domain node (tag ccn1); isotropic, diagonal or full tensor, normally From material.

parameters.name: Terminal / Ground / Electric Potential
parameters.description: Boundary nodes that drive the problem; Zero Charge is the default exterior condition.

parameters.name: Terminal sweep
parameters.description: Interface-level option that automatically sweeps each terminal to extract a full capacitance or admittance matrix.

parameters.name: Discretization
parameters.description: Shape-function order for V; Quadratic is the default.

tools.notes: Ships in the core COMSOL Multiphysics package; the AC/DC Module adds terminals with lumped parameter extraction, electric circuits, charge relaxation and the advanced material models. Related: Electric Currents (ec), Electrostatics, Boundary Elements (esbe) for open regions without meshing the surroundings, and the Electrostatics-Solid Mechanics couplings used for MEMS.

tools.name: Electric Currents (ec)
tools.description: Solves current conservation, -div(sigma*grad(V) + J_e) = Q, for the potential in conducting media, giving the current density J = sigma*E and the resistive loss density ec.Qh. In the frequency domain it also carries displacement currents, so it covers both DC resistive and AC impedance problems. Use it for busbars, resistive heaters, ECG/EIT electrode problems, grounding grids, PCB traces and as the electrical half of a Joule heating model; the loss variable ec.Qh is exactly what the Electromagnetic Heating coupling feeds into the heat equation.
tools.usage: Model Wizard / Add Physics > AC/DC > Electric Fields and Currents > Electric Currents (ec)

parameters.name: Electrical conductivity sigma
parameters.description: On the Current Conservation domain node; typically temperature dependent for a heating model.

parameters.name: Terminal type
parameters.description: Voltage, Current, Circuit, Power or Terminated - sets what is prescribed on an electrode.

parameters.name: V0 / I0 / P0
parameters.description: The prescribed terminal value matching the terminal type.

parameters.name: Electric Insulation
parameters.description: Default exterior boundary condition, n.J = 0.

tools.notes: Ships in the core package; the AC/DC Module adds the Electric Currents, Shell interface for thin conducting layers, electric circuits and lumped parameter extraction. Every model needs exactly one ground (or at least one voltage-type terminal) or the potential is undefined up to a constant.

tools.name: Magnetic Fields (mf)
tools.description: Solves Ampere's law in terms of the magnetic vector potential A, curl(mu^-1 curl A) + sigma*dA/dt = J_e, using curl (edge) elements so that the tangential continuity of A is enforced exactly. It handles static, time-dependent and frequency-domain problems including eddy currents, skin effect, proximity effect and induced losses. Use it for inductors, transformers, motors, magnetic actuators, induction heating, magnetic shielding and non-destructive testing; when there are no currents at all, the scalar-potential interface Magnetic Fields, No Currents (mfnc) is far cheaper.
tools.usage: Model Wizard / Add Physics > AC/DC > Electromagnetic Fields > Magnetic Fields (mf)

parameters.name: Constitutive relation
parameters.description: On the Ampere's Law domain node: relative permeability, B-H curve, remanent flux density, magnetization or an effective nonlinear model.

parameters.name: Magnetic Insulation
parameters.description: Default exterior boundary condition, n x A = 0, which makes the boundary a flux line.

parameters.name: Gauge fixing for A-field
parameters.description: Adds a scalar Lagrange multiplier that removes the null space of the curl operator; often needed for stationary and low-frequency solves.

parameters.name: Infinite Element Domain
parameters.description: A Definitions node that stretches an outer shell to infinity so the far field decays correctly without a huge air box.

tools.notes: Requires the AC/DC Module. Always model the surrounding air and terminate it with Magnetic Insulation, an Infinite Element Domain or a symmetry condition. Related interfaces: Magnetic and Electric Fields (mef) for voltage-driven conductors where A and V are solved together, Magnetic Fields, Currents Only, Rotating Machinery Magnetic, and the Electrical Circuit interface for SPICE-style coupling.

tools.name: Magnetic Fields, No Currents (mfnc)
tools.description: Solves the magnetostatic problem with a scalar magnetic potential Vm, -div(mu0*mu_r*grad(Vm) - B_r) = 0, valid in current-free regions. Because there is a single scalar unknown instead of a vector potential, it is an order of magnitude cheaper than Magnetic Fields and has no gauge problem. Use it for permanent-magnet assemblies, magnetic circuits, magnetic levitation and recording heads, magnetic separators and magnetometer shielding - anywhere the sources are magnets or prescribed magnetization rather than currents.
tools.usage: Model Wizard / Add Physics > AC/DC > Magnetic Fields, No Currents (mfnc)

parameters.name: Magnetic flux conservation
parameters.description: Domain node with the constitutive relation: relative permeability, B-H curve, remanent flux density B_r, or magnetization M.

parameters.name: Magnetic Insulation / Magnetic Flux Density
parameters.description: Boundary conditions; Magnetic Insulation (n.B = 0) is the default exterior condition.

parameters.name: Zero Magnetic Scalar Potential
parameters.description: Point or boundary condition needed to pin the potential level in a fully insulated model.

parameters.name: Force Calculation
parameters.description: Subnode that integrates the Maxwell stress tensor to give the net force and torque on a magnet or pole piece.

tools.notes: Requires the AC/DC Module. Do not use it if any domain carries a net current - the scalar potential is multivalued around a current-carrying conductor. For permanent magnets combined with coils, use Magnetic Fields (mf) or the mixed scalar/vector formulation instead.

tools.name: Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain (emw)
tools.description: Solves the vector Helmholtz (wave) equation curl(mu_r^-1 curl E) - k0^2*(epsilon_r - j*sigma/(omega*eps0))*E = 0 for the time-harmonic electric field, discretized with curl elements. It supports frequency-domain, eigenfrequency (resonant modes), mode analysis (waveguide propagation constants) and frequency-domain-modal studies, plus full-wave scattering with a background field. Use it for antennas, waveguides, filters, resonators, RF connectors, microwave heating, metamaterials, RCS and nanophotonic scattering - anything where the device is comparable in size to the wavelength.
tools.usage: Model Wizard / Add Physics > Radio Frequency > Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain (emw)

parameters.name: Electric field components solved for
parameters.description: Three-component (full vector), out-of-plane or in-plane vector in 2D.

parameters.name: Formulation / Solve for
parameters.description: Full field or Scattered field, where an incoming Background Electric Field is prescribed and only the scattered part is solved.

parameters.name: Wave Equation, Electric
parameters.description: Domain node holding epsilon_r, mu_r, sigma or the refractive index n and k.

parameters.name: Port / Lumped Port / Periodic Condition
parameters.description: Excitation and de-embedding nodes that also generate S-parameters.

parameters.name: Perfect Electric Conductor / Impedance Boundary Condition
parameters.description: Boundary conditions for lossless metal (n x E = 0) and for good-but-lossy metal thicker than the skin depth.

tools.notes: Requires the RF Module (or the Wave Optics Module for the same interface aimed at optical wavelengths). Mesh at least five elements per wavelength in every material - the wavelength shrinks by sqrt(epsilon_r) inside a dielectric. Related interfaces: Electromagnetic Waves, Transient (temw) for nonlinear or pulsed problems, Electromagnetic Waves, Beam Envelopes (ewbe) for long optical structures where only the slowly varying envelope is resolved, and Geometrical Optics (gop) from the Ray Optics Module when the geometry is thousands of wavelengths across.

tools.name: Terminal
tools.description: Drives an electrode in Electrostatics or Electric Currents by a prescribed voltage, current, power, external circuit connection or terminated (matched) impedance, while keeping the whole boundary at a single equipotential. It also declares the lumped quantities that COMSOL uses to build capacitance, admittance and impedance matrices when a terminal sweep is enabled. Use one Terminal per electrode and at least one Ground; prefer Terminal over Electric Potential whenever you want current, charge, capacitance or an external circuit connection reported automatically.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Electric Currents (ec) > right-click > Terminal (also under Electrostatics, Electric Currents Shell, and the electrochemistry interfaces)

parameters.name: Terminal type
parameters.description: Voltage, Current, Circuit, Power, Terminated or Charge (Electrostatics).

parameters.name: V0 / I0 / P_in
parameters.description: The prescribed value corresponding to the terminal type.

parameters.name: Terminal name
parameters.description: Integer label used to identify the terminal in the capacitance/impedance matrix and in circuit connections.

parameters.name: Ground
parameters.description: Companion node setting V = 0; every model needs at least one ground or terminal-type voltage reference.

parameters.name: Floating Potential
parameters.description: Related node for an isolated conductor whose potential is unknown but uniform, optionally carrying a prescribed net charge or current.

tools.notes: Terminal with lumped parameter extraction and circuit coupling requires the AC/DC Module. To get a capacitance matrix, number the terminals 1..N and add a Stationary Source Sweep study step (or enable Terminal sweep on the interface); the result appears under Results > Derived Values as es.C11, es.C12 and so on.

tools.name: Coil (Homogenized Multiturn)
tools.description: Models a winding of many thin turns as a homogenized current distribution, so the individual wires never need to be meshed: the node spreads the total current I*N over the coil cross-section along a prescribed direction and reports the induced voltage, inductance and losses. Conductor models are Single conductor (a solid massive conductor with eddy currents resolved) and Homogenized multiturn (a bundle of N insulated turns with a fill factor). Use it for inductors, transformer windings, motor coils, magnetic actuators and induction heaters; the Coil Geometry Analysis study step first works out the current path in 3D closed loops.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Magnetic Fields (mf) > right-click > Coil (add a Coil Geometry Analysis study step for 3D coils)

parameters.name: Conductor model
parameters.description: Single conductor or Homogenized multiturn.

parameters.name: Number of turns N
parameters.description: Turn count of the homogenized winding.

parameters.name: Coil excitation
parameters.description: Current, Voltage, Power or Circuit (coupled to the Electrical Circuit interface).

parameters.name: ICoil / VCoil
parameters.description: Prescribed coil current or voltage.

parameters.name: Coil wire cross-section area / conductivity
parameters.description: Used to compute ohmic losses and the coil resistance in the homogenized model.

parameters.name: Coil geometry (subnodes)
parameters.description: Linear, Circular, Numeric or User defined current direction; the Numeric option runs a small auxiliary problem to find the current path.

tools.notes: Requires the AC/DC Module. In 3D, a closed homogenized coil needs a Coil Geometry Analysis study step before the main study, otherwise the current direction is undefined. Results variables include mf.ICoil_1, mf.VCoil_1 and mf.LCoil_1 (self-inductance). For a resolved-strand winding with proximity losses, use Single conductor coils or the Coil Group option instead.

tools.name: Lumped Port
tools.description: Excites and terminates a transmission-line-like feed that is electrically small compared with the wavelength - a coaxial feed gap, a microstrip edge, a slot or a discrete component gap - by relating the voltage across the gap to the current through it with a chosen characteristic impedance. It generates S-parameters, port voltage and current, and can be set as a passive load or an active source. Use it for antenna feeds and lumped RF components; use the full Port node when the feed is a real waveguide cross-section whose mode shape must be computed.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain (emw) > right-click > Lumped Port

parameters.name: Type of lumped port
parameters.description: Uniform, Coaxial, or User defined with an explicit height, width and direction.

parameters.name: Terminal type
parameters.description: Cable (voltage source with characteristic impedance Z_ref), Current, or Circuit.

parameters.name: Characteristic impedance Zref
parameters.description: Reference impedance for the S-parameter calculation, normally 50 ohm.

parameters.name: Wave excitation at this port
parameters.description: On for the driving port, Off for passive ports; only one port is usually active at a time.

parameters.name: Port name
parameters.description: Integer used to label the S-parameter entries emw.S11, emw.S21 and so on.

tools.notes: Requires the RF Module. The lumped-port approximation breaks down when the gap approaches a tenth of a wavelength - switch to a Port with a numeric or analytic mode then. Use a Port Sweep (under the study) to get the full S-matrix in one run, and remember that S-parameters are only meaningful when every port is either excited or matched.

tools.name: Scattering Boundary Condition
tools.description: First- or second-order absorbing boundary condition for wave electromagnetics that lets an outgoing plane, cylindrical or spherical wave leave the domain with little reflection, and can simultaneously launch an incident wave. Mathematically it is a Robin condition n.grad(E) + j*k0*E = 0 (plus a tangential-Laplacian term for the second-order form), so it costs nothing extra in degrees of freedom. Use it as a cheap open boundary when the wave hits the boundary close to normal incidence; for strongly oblique or evanescent fields a Perfectly Matched Layer absorbs far better.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Electromagnetic Waves, Frequency Domain (emw) > right-click > Scattering Boundary Condition

parameters.name: Order
parameters.description: First order or Second order; the second-order form keeps reflection below a few percent out to roughly 75 degrees of incidence.

parameters.name: Incident field
parameters.description: No incident field, Wave given by E field, or Wave given by H field - this is how a plane wave is launched into the domain.

parameters.name: Incident wave direction k_dir
parameters.description: Propagation direction of the incident wave.

parameters.name: Scattered wave type
parameters.description: Plane wave, Cylindrical wave, Spherical wave, or a user-defined phase reference point.

tools.notes: Requires the RF Module or the Wave Optics Module. The exact API type string for this node is deliberately not quoted here - record the action with File > Save As > Model File for Java (or Compact History) to capture it for your version. Place the boundary at least a quarter wavelength (ideally half) from the scatterer, and prefer a Perfectly Matched Layer for antenna far fields or when the boundary cannot be kept far away.

tools.name: Perfectly Matched Layer
tools.description: A domain-level absorbing layer defined under Component > Definitions that applies a complex coordinate stretching to the selected shell of elements, so waves entering it decay exponentially and essentially nothing reflects back, at any angle of incidence. It is a coordinate-system feature, so the same PML works for electromagnetic, acoustic, elastic and thermoviscous waves - each physics interface picks up the stretching automatically. Use it to truncate an open domain for antennas, radiation, scattering and free-field acoustics, wrapping the physical region in a shell of typically 5 to 8 swept or mapped element layers.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Definitions > right-click > Perfectly Matched Layer, then select the PML domains (build them as a geometry Layer or a surrounding shell)

parameters.name: Geometry type
parameters.description: Cartesian, Cylindrical, Spherical or User defined - must match the shape of the PML shell.

parameters.name: Coordinate stretching type
parameters.description: Polynomial (default), Rational or User defined stretching function.

parameters.name: PML scaling factor and curvature parameter
parameters.description: Control how aggressively the coordinate is stretched; the defaults work for most wave problems.

parameters.name: Typical wavelength from
parameters.description: Physics interface or a user-defined wavelength, used to scale the absorption; set it explicitly when one PML serves two physics with different wavelengths.

tools.notes: A PML is a mesh-quality feature as much as a physics one: use a structured (swept or mapped) mesh with the elements aligned with the absorbing direction, or the numerical reflection rises sharply. PMLs work only for propagating waves - they do not help in a stationary or low-frequency magnetostatic model, where an Infinite Element Domain is the right tool instead. Related: Scattering Boundary Condition, Impedance Boundary Condition, Far-Field Calculation.

tools.name: Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain (acpr)
tools.description: Solves the Helmholtz equation div(-(1/rho_c)(grad p - q_d)) - k_eq^2*p/rho_c = Q_m for the time-harmonic acoustic pressure in a quiescent fluid, with complex-valued density and speed of sound to represent damping, porous absorbers and narrow-region losses. Study types include Frequency Domain, Eigenfrequency (room and cavity modes), Mode Analysis and Boundary Mode Analysis. Use it for loudspeakers, mufflers, sonar, ultrasound transducers, room and car-cabin acoustics, and as the fluid half of vibroacoustic models; it is the most-used acoustics interface by a wide margin.
tools.usage: Model Wizard / Add Physics > Acoustics > Pressure Acoustics > Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain (acpr)

parameters.name: Fluid model
parameters.description: Linear elastic, Linear elastic with attenuation, Thermally conducting and/or viscous, Ideal gas, or one of the poroacoustic models (Delany-Bazley-Miki, Johnson-Champoux-Allard, Zwikker-Kosten).

parameters.name: Speed of sound c and density rho
parameters.description: Taken from the fluid material; complex values encode attenuation.

parameters.name: Sound Hard Boundary (Wall)
parameters.description: Default exterior condition, n.grad(p) = 0.

parameters.name: Pressure / Normal Acceleration / Impedance / Interior Sound Hard
parameters.description: Boundary sources and loads: prescribed pressure, a vibrating surface, a lumped surface impedance, or an internal rigid baffle.

parameters.name: Plane Wave Radiation / Spherical Wave Radiation
parameters.description: Non-reflecting conditions for an open boundary, optionally with an incident wave.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Mesh with at least 5-6 second-order elements per wavelength at the highest frequency in the sweep, which is what makes high-frequency acoustics expensive. For an exterior radiation problem add a Perfectly Matched Layer plus an Exterior Field Calculation node to get the far-field directivity. Related: Pressure Acoustics, Boundary Elements (no volume mesh needed outside), Acoustic Diffusion Equation and Ray Acoustics for high-frequency room acoustics.

tools.name: Pressure Acoustics, Transient (actd)
tools.description: Time-domain counterpart of acpr: it solves the scalar wave equation (1/(rho*c^2))*d2p/dt2 + div(-(1/rho)(grad p - q_d)) = Q_m for transient acoustic pressure, so pulses, nonlinear propagation (Westervelt), time-varying sources and broadband excitation can be modelled directly. Version 6.3 added GPU-accelerated solving for time-domain pressure acoustics with the discontinuous Galerkin (time explicit) variant. Use it for ultrasound pulses, sonar pings, impulse responses, transient loudspeaker behaviour, and any case where the excitation is not a single frequency.
tools.usage: Model Wizard / Add Physics > Acoustics > Pressure Acoustics > Pressure Acoustics, Transient (actd)

parameters.name: Transient solver settings
parameters.description: Time step and the CFL condition - the step must resolve the highest frequency of interest, typically at least 20 steps per period.

parameters.name: Fluid model
parameters.description: Linear elastic, or the Westervelt nonlinear model for high-amplitude ultrasound.

parameters.name: Sound Hard Boundary / Sound Soft Boundary
parameters.description: Rigid wall (default) and pressure-release boundary.

parameters.name: Plane Wave Radiation
parameters.description: Time-domain non-reflecting boundary; a PML also works in the transient case.

parameters.name: Normal Acceleration / Normal Velocity
parameters.description: Time-dependent surface excitation, typically driven by an analytic pulse or a Ramp / Gaussian pulse function.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Time-domain acoustics is memory- and time-hungry: the mesh must resolve the shortest wavelength in the excitation spectrum and the time step must satisfy the CFL condition, so use the Time Explicit (dG-FEM) interfaces for large high-frequency models. Check the create() type string against a recorded Java file if your version differs.

tools.name: Thermoviscous Acoustics, Frequency Domain (ta)
tools.description: Solves the full linearized Navier-Stokes, continuity and energy equations for acoustic pressure, particle velocity and temperature variation simultaneously, so the viscous and thermal boundary layers at walls are resolved explicitly. This matters whenever a geometric dimension is comparable to the boundary-layer thickness (a fraction of a millimetre in air at audio frequencies). Use it for MEMS microphones and speakers, hearing aids, mobile-phone acoustics, perforated plates and narrow slits, and small transducers; elsewhere the far cheaper Pressure Acoustics with a narrow-region-acoustics correction is enough.
tools.usage: Model Wizard / Add Physics > Acoustics > Thermoviscous Acoustics > Thermoviscous Acoustics, Frequency Domain (ta)

parameters.name: Thermoviscous Acoustics Model
parameters.description: Domain node with dynamic and bulk viscosity, thermal conductivity, heat capacity and the equation of state.

parameters.name: No Slip / Isothermal
parameters.description: Default wall conditions, u = 0 and T = T0, which is what creates the boundary layers.

parameters.name: Boundary Layer Mesh
parameters.description: Meshing requirement: several elements across the viscous penetration depth ta.d_visc at the lowest frequency.

parameters.name: Mechanical / Thermal boundary conditions
parameters.description: Velocity, Slip, Adiabatic, Interior Wall and Thermoviscous Acoustics-Structure boundary couplings.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Three or four dependent variables per node make this the most expensive acoustics interface - restrict it to the small region that needs it and couple it to Pressure Acoustics elsewhere with the Acoustic-Thermoviscous Acoustic Boundary multiphysics coupling. Related: Thermoviscous Acoustics, Transient, Thermoviscous Acoustics, Boundary Mode, and the SLNS Approximation interface which is a cheaper approximation of the same physics. Verify the create() type string against a recorded Java file.

tools.name: Transport of Diluted Species (tds)
tools.description: Solves the convection-diffusion-reaction equation dc_i/dt + div(-D_i*grad(c_i)) + u.grad(c_i) = R_i for one or more dilute solutes in a solvent, optionally with electromigration (Nernst-Planck) when a potential field is present. Domain nodes cover free media, porous media (with retardation and adsorption isotherms) and fractures; boundary nodes give inflow concentrations, outflow, fluxes, reactions and partition conditions. Use it for mixing and residence time, chemical reactors, drug delivery, pollutant transport, sensors, chromatography and microfluidic assays - anywhere the species do not change the bulk fluid properties.
tools.usage: Model Wizard / Add Physics > Chemical Species Transport > Transport of Diluted Species (tds)

parameters.name: Number of species / Concentrations
parameters.description: Dependent variable names, one per transported species (c, c2, ...).

parameters.name: Diffusion coefficient D_c
parameters.description: Isotropic or tensor diffusivity on the Transport Properties node.

parameters.name: Velocity field u
parameters.description: User defined, or coupled to a flow interface via the Reacting Flow / Flow Coupling multiphysics node.

parameters.name: Reactions R
parameters.description: Domain node with the volumetric rate expression, or supplied by a Chemistry (chem) interface.

parameters.name: Inflow / Outflow / Flux / No Flux
parameters.description: Boundary nodes; No Flux is the default exterior condition and Outflow imposes zero diffusive flux.

tools.notes: A basic version ships in the core package; the Chemical Reaction Engineering Module, Battery Design Module, Porous Media Flow Module and Microfluidics Module extend it with porous media, migration and reaction coupling. Convection-dominated transport (high Peclet number) needs either a fine mesh or the built-in streamline and crosswind stabilization - check for over- and undershoots around sharp fronts. Related: Transport of Concentrated Species, Nernst-Planck Equations, Surface Reactions.

tools.name: Reaction Engineering (re)
tools.description: A zero-dimensional (well-mixed) interface for reaction kinetics and reactor energy balances: you type reaction formulas such as "A + 2B => C", and COMSOL derives the rate expressions, species mass balances and, with thermodynamics enabled, the heat of reaction and temperature dependence. Reactor models include batch, continuous stirred tank (constant volume or pressure), semibatch and plug flow. Use it to fit kinetics against experimental data and to size a reactor quickly, then use Generate Space-Dependent Model to export the same chemistry into a 2D or 3D Transport of Diluted Species plus flow model.
tools.usage: Model Wizard / Add Physics > Chemical Species Transport > Reaction Engineering (re) (added in a 0D component), then right-click > Reaction to enter each reaction formula

parameters.name: Reaction formula
parameters.description: Text such as "2H2 + O2 => 2H2O"; COMSOL parses stoichiometry and generates rate terms automatically.

parameters.name: Reaction type / rate constants
parameters.description: Elementary (mass action) or user defined, with Arrhenius parameters A, n and E for temperature dependence.

parameters.name: Reactor type
parameters.description: Batch, Batch constant volume, CSTR constant volume/mass, Semibatch or Plug flow.

parameters.name: Energy balance
parameters.description: Isothermal, Non-isothermal (with heat of reaction) or Thermally insulated; requires species enthalpy data.

parameters.name: Generate Space-Dependent Model
parameters.description: Node that exports the kinetics, species and thermodynamics into a spatial component with tds/spf/ht interfaces.

tools.notes: Requires the Chemical Reaction Engineering Module. The companion Chemistry (chem) interface holds the same kinetics and thermodynamic property package but is used directly inside a space-dependent component, supplying reaction rates and mixture properties to tds, spf and ht. Reaction Engineering lives in a 0D component, so the create() call and geometry differ from the other interfaces - record a Java file to get the exact form.

tools.name: Secondary Current Distribution
tools.description: Electrochemical cell interface that solves for the electrolyte and electrode potentials assuming a uniform electrolyte composition, with the electrode kinetics entering through activation overpotential expressions (Butler-Volmer, Tafel, linearized or user defined). It is the middle member of the family: Primary Current Distribution ignores kinetics entirely (ohmic drop only), Secondary adds activation losses, and Tertiary Current Distribution, Nernst-Planck also resolves concentration gradients. Use it for electroplating and electrodeposition cells, cathodic protection and corrosion, electrolysers, fuel cells and battery cell design where mass transport is not limiting.
tools.usage: Model Wizard / Add Physics > Electrochemistry > Primary and Secondary Current Distribution > Secondary Current Distribution, then right-click > Electrode Surface / Electrode Reaction

parameters.name: Electrolyte conductivity sigma_l
parameters.description: On the Electrolyte domain node; the ohmic drop through the solution.

parameters.name: Electrode conductivity sigma_s
parameters.description: On the Electrode domain node for the metal phase.

parameters.name: Equilibrium potential Eeq
parameters.description: Reference potential of each electrode reaction.

parameters.name: Exchange current density i0
parameters.description: Kinetics parameter of the Butler-Volmer expression, together with the anodic and cathodic transfer coefficients.

parameters.name: Electrode Surface / Electrolyte Current Density / Electric Ground
parameters.description: Boundary nodes that set the cell terminals and the reacting interfaces.

tools.notes: Requires the Electrodeposition Module, Corrosion Module, Fuel Cell & Electrolyzer Module, Battery Design Module or Electrochemistry Module depending on the application; the Corrosion and Electrodeposition modules add dedicated deposition, dissolution and deforming-geometry nodes. Related interfaces: Lithium-Ion Battery (liion) for porous-electrode battery models, Tertiary Current Distribution, Nernst-Planck, and Electroanalysis. The default physics tag is assigned when the interface is added - read it from the Name field of the Settings window before scripting.

tools.name: Semiconductor (semi)
tools.description: Solves the drift-diffusion equations - Poisson's equation for the electrostatic potential coupled to the electron and hole continuity equations with drift and diffusion currents - using either a finite-element or finite-volume discretization. Doping, generation-recombination (SRH, Auger, direct, impact ionization), incomplete ionization, band-gap narrowing and trap-assisted models are all available, and Fermi-Dirac statistics can replace Maxwell-Boltzmann. Use it for diodes, MOSFETs, BJTs, IGBTs, solar cells, photodiodes, LEDs and semiconductor optoelectronics; it is often coupled to Heat Transfer for self-heating or to the wave-optics interfaces for photonic devices.
tools.usage: Model Wizard / Add Physics > Semiconductor > Semiconductor (semi)

parameters.name: Semiconductor Material Model
parameters.description: Domain node with band gap, effective density of states, mobilities and the carrier statistics model.

parameters.name: Analytic Doping Model / Geometric Doping Model
parameters.description: Subnodes defining the doping profile as a box, Gaussian or user-defined function, or from a distance-to-boundary function.

parameters.name: Metal Contact
parameters.description: Boundary node for ohmic, Schottky, ideal or thin-insulator-gate contacts, with a voltage, current or circuit terminal.

parameters.name: Trap-Assisted Recombination / Auger Recombination / Impact Ionization
parameters.description: Generation-recombination subnodes.

parameters.name: Discretization
parameters.description: Finite element (with log or quasi-Fermi formulation) or Finite volume, which is usually more robust for strongly nonlinear devices.

tools.notes: Requires the Semiconductor Module. Drift-diffusion is strongly nonlinear over many orders of magnitude in carrier density, so ramp the bias with an auxiliary sweep from zero and use the finite-volume discretization when the Newton solver struggles. Related: Semiconductor Optoelectronics (Beam Envelopes and Frequency Domain) and the Schrodinger Equation interface for quantum-confined structures.

tools.name: Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow (fpt)
tools.description: Integrates Newton's second law for a large number of discrete particles moving through a previously computed (or simultaneously solved) fluid velocity field, with force nodes for drag (Stokes, Schiller-Naumann, Haider-Levenspiel and others), gravity, buoyancy, lift, Brownian motion, electric, magnetic, dielectrophoretic, magnetophoretic, acoustophoretic and thermophoretic forces. Wall conditions include freeze, bounce, stick, disappear and a user-defined sticking probability. Use it for filters and separators, cyclones, spray and aerosol deposition, mass spectrometers, inkjet drops, particle sorting in microfluidics and residence-time distributions.
tools.usage: Model Wizard / Add Physics > Fluid Flow > Particle Tracing > Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow (fpt); solve the flow first, then add a Time Dependent study with a Particle Tracing solver

parameters.name: Particle release specification
parameters.description: Specify release times (particles released during the time-dependent solve) or Specify current (a steady stream with an associated current/mass flow).

parameters.name: Inlet / Release from Grid / Release from Data File
parameters.description: Nodes defining where and how particles enter, including initial position and velocity distributions.

parameters.name: Drag Force
parameters.description: Force node with the drag law, fluid velocity field u, viscosity and particle diameter dp.

parameters.name: Wall
parameters.description: Boundary node with Freeze, Bounce, Stick, Disappear, Pass through or a probabilistic condition.

parameters.name: Particle-field interaction
parameters.description: One-way coupling (default, fluid unaffected) or bidirectionally coupled particle tracing when the particle load changes the flow.

tools.notes: Requires the Particle Tracing Module. Particle tracing uses a dedicated Time Dependent solver and a separate Particle dataset in Results (Particle Trajectories plot, Poincare maps, phase portraits). Related interfaces: Charged Particle Tracing, Mathematical Particle Tracing, and the Plasma Module interfaces (Plasma (plas), Drift Diffusion, Capacitively/Inductively Coupled Plasma) for ionized gases.

tools.name: Coefficient Form PDE (c)
tools.description: A Mathematics interface that exposes a general second-order PDE in coefficient form, e_a*d2u/dt2 + d_a*du/dt + div(-c*grad(u) - alpha*u + gamma) + beta.grad(u) + a*u = f, where every coefficient is a field you type in. Boundary conditions are the matching Dirichlet, Flux/Source and Neumann nodes. Use it to implement an equation COMSOL does not ship - custom diffusion, wave, Helmholtz, Schrodinger or population models - or to add an extra scalar field that couples to a standard physics interface; it supports systems of equations by increasing the number of dependent variables.
tools.usage: Model Wizard / Add Physics > Mathematics > PDE Interfaces > Coefficient Form PDE (c)

parameters.name: Dependent variables
parameters.description: Number and names of the unknown fields; a vector of n components gives a coupled system with matrix coefficients.

parameters.name: c
parameters.description: Diffusion coefficient (scalar, matrix or tensor per component).

parameters.name: a and f
parameters.description: Absorption coefficient and source term.

parameters.name: e_a and d_a
parameters.description: Mass and damping coefficients, which select stationary, first-order or second-order transient behaviour.

parameters.name: alpha, beta, gamma
parameters.description: Conservative and convection flux coefficients and the conservative flux source.

parameters.name: Units
parameters.description: Source term quantity and dependent variable quantity - set them so that COMSOL's unit checking stays meaningful.

tools.notes: Ships in the core COMSOL Multiphysics package. The default Zero Flux condition means that any boundary you do not touch is insulating. Related Mathematics interfaces: General Form PDE (g) when the equation cannot be written in coefficient form, Wave Form PDE, Weak Form PDE (w) for direct entry of the weak expression, Domain ODEs and DAEs (dode) for pointwise equations with no spatial derivatives, and Events for discrete state changes.

tools.name: General Form PDE (g)
tools.description: Mathematics interface for a PDE written as e_a*d2u/dt2 + d_a*du/dt + div(Gamma) = f, where the flux vector Gamma and the source f are arbitrary expressions of u, its gradient, the coordinates and any other model variable. Because the coefficients need not be linear in u, this is the interface for genuinely nonlinear custom equations - nonlinear diffusion, reaction fronts, custom constitutive laws - and COMSOL differentiates the expressions symbolically to build the Jacobian. Boundary conditions are Dirichlet and Flux/Source nodes matching the flux Gamma.
tools.usage: Model Wizard / Add Physics > Mathematics > PDE Interfaces > General Form PDE (g)

parameters.name: Conservative flux Gamma
parameters.description: Vector expression, for example {-D(u)*ux, -D(u)*uy, -D(u)*uz} for concentration-dependent diffusion.

parameters.name: Source term f
parameters.description: Right-hand side, which may depend nonlinearly on u.

parameters.name: Damping or mass coefficient d_a
parameters.description: Multiplies du/dt for a first-order transient problem.

parameters.name: Mass coefficient e_a
parameters.description: Multiplies d2u/dt2 for a wave-type problem.

parameters.name: Zero Flux / Flux-Source / Dirichlet Boundary Condition
parameters.description: Boundary nodes; Zero Flux (n.Gamma = 0) is the default.

tools.notes: Ships in the core package. Inside the expressions, ux, uy and uz are the built-in spatial derivatives of the dependent variable u. A boundary-only variant, General Form Boundary PDE, solves the same kind of equation on a surface - useful for surface diffusion and membrane transport. Give a good initial value: a nonlinear General Form PDE has no automatic continuation.

tools.name: Global ODEs and DAEs (ge)
tools.description: Adds space-independent (global) unknowns governed by ordinary differential or algebraic equations written in residual form f(u, du/dt, d2u/dt2, t) = 0. The equations can reference any model quantity - an integral over a boundary, a probe, a coupling operator - so this is how you attach a lumped model (control loop, external circuit, reservoir mass balance, PID controller, prescribed total force) to a distributed PDE model. Use it for closed-loop control of a simulation, lumped-parameter subsystems, integral constraints and any unknown scalar the solver must find alongside the fields.
tools.usage: Model Wizard / Add Physics > Mathematics > ODE and DAE Interfaces > Global ODEs and DAEs (ge), then edit the Global Equations table

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: Name of the global dependent variable, for example "T_ctrl" or "Q".

parameters.name: f(u,ut,utt,t)
parameters.description: Residual expression that the solver drives to zero; it may contain integration coupling operators such as intop1(...).

parameters.name: Initial value (u_0) and (u_t0)
parameters.description: Starting value and starting time derivative for a transient solve.

parameters.name: Description / Units
parameters.description: Dependent variable quantity and source term quantity, needed for unit consistency.

tools.notes: Ships in the core package. Related interfaces: Domain ODEs and DAEs (pointwise equations on a domain - useful for damage and history variables), Boundary ODEs and DAEs, Events for discrete switching, and the Optimization and Sensitivity study steps (Optimization Module) when the extra unknown is a design variable rather than a state. Watch the units: a mismatched source-term unit produces an inconsistent-units warning rather than an error.

tools.name: Thermal Expansion (multiphysics coupling)
tools.description: Multiphysics node that joins a Heat Transfer interface to a structural interface: it takes the computed temperature field, forms the thermal strain epsilon_th = alpha*(T - T_ref), subtracts it from the total strain so the stress is computed from the elastic part only, and (in the two-way form) adds the thermoelastic damping term back to the heat equation. Use it for thermal stress in electronics packages, bimetallic actuators, brake discs, welds, turbine parts and anywhere a temperature gradient causes deformation. The pair Heat Transfer in Solids + Solid Mechanics + this coupling is what Add Physics > Structural Mechanics > Thermal-Structure Interaction > Thermal Stress builds in one step.
tools.usage: Component 1 > Multiphysics > right-click > Thermal Expansion (after adding both a heat transfer and a structural interface), or use the Thermal Stress predefined multiphysics interface

parameters.name: Coefficient of thermal expansion alpha
parameters.description: Secant or tangent CTE, isotropic or tensor, usually From material.

parameters.name: Strain reference temperature Tref
parameters.description: Temperature at which the structure is stress free; a wrong value silently biases all the stresses.

parameters.name: Structural interface / Heat transfer interface
parameters.description: The two interfaces being coupled, selected in the coupling node.

parameters.name: Thermal expansion model
parameters.description: Secant coefficient of thermal expansion, tangent coefficient, or thermal strain entered directly as a function of T.

tools.notes: The create() signature for a multiphysics node is (tag, type, geometry tag, entity dimension); -1 means the coupling is global rather than tied to a geometric entity. Temperature Coupling simply maps T from the source interface into the destination interface and is often added automatically alongside Thermal Expansion. A one-way analysis (solve heat first, then structure) is much cheaper than a fully coupled solve and is usually sufficient unless the deformation changes the thermal path.

tools.name: Electromagnetic Heating / Joule Heating
tools.description: Multiphysics coupling that sends the resistive and dielectric loss density computed by an electromagnetic interface into a Heat Transfer interface as a volumetric heat source, and sends the temperature back so that the electrical conductivity and permittivity follow their temperature dependence. The predefined Joule Heating interface bundles Electric Currents (ec) + Heat Transfer (ht) + this coupling; Induction Heating uses Magnetic Fields, Microwave Heating uses Electromagnetic Waves and Laser Heating uses Beam Envelopes. Use it for busbars and fuses, resistive heaters, induction hardening, RF ablation, microwave ovens and laser processing.
tools.usage: Model Wizard / Add Physics > Heat Transfer > Electromagnetic Heating > Joule Heating (adds ec, ht and the coupling), or Component 1 > Multiphysics > right-click > Electromagnetic Heating

parameters.name: Electromagnetic interface / Heat transfer interface
parameters.description: The two interfaces being coupled.

parameters.name: Boundary electromagnetic heat source
parameters.description: Companion node that applies surface losses (from an Impedance Boundary Condition or a thin conducting layer) as a boundary heat source.

parameters.name: Temperature-dependent conductivity
parameters.description: Set on the electromagnetic material, typically sigma = sigma0/(1 + alpha*(T - T0)); this is what makes the coupling two-way.

parameters.name: Study type
parameters.description: Stationary, Time Dependent, or Frequency-Stationary / Frequency-Transient when the electromagnetic part is harmonic and the thermal part is not.

tools.notes: Joule heating with Electric Currents ships in the core package; induction, microwave and laser heating need the AC/DC, RF or Wave Optics Module together with the Heat Transfer Module. When the electromagnetic problem is time-harmonic and the thermal problem is slow, use a Frequency-Stationary or Frequency-Transient study step so the field is solved at the operating frequency while the temperature marches in time. The loss variable is ec.Qh (or mf.Qh, emw.Qh).

tools.name: Fluid-Structure Interaction
tools.description: Multiphysics coupling that applies the fluid's total stress (pressure plus viscous traction) as a load on a structural boundary and feeds the structural velocity back to the fluid as a moving-wall condition, with the fluid mesh deformed by a Moving Mesh (ALE) node so the flow domain follows the structure. Use it for valves and check valves, flow-induced vibration, flapping and peristaltic devices, blood vessels, MEMS resonators in a fluid and pressure-driven membranes. COMSOL also offers a fixed-geometry variant for small deformations and a Fluid-Multibody Interaction, Assembly variant for rigid bodies on joints.
tools.usage: Model Wizard / Add Physics > Fluid Flow > Fluid-Structure Interaction > Fluid-Solid Interaction (adds spf, solid, the moving mesh and the coupling), or Component 1 > Multiphysics > right-click > Fluid-Structure Interaction

parameters.name: Fluid interface / Structure interface
parameters.description: The flow and structural interfaces being coupled.

parameters.name: Coupled interface boundaries
parameters.description: The wetted boundaries where traction and velocity are exchanged.

parameters.name: Fluid-structure interaction type
parameters.description: Fully coupled (two-way), Fluid loading on structure only, or Velocity transfer to fluid only - one-way options are far cheaper.

parameters.name: Moving mesh / Deforming Domain
parameters.description: Smoothing type (Laplace, Winslow, hyperelastic) and the mesh-slip settings that keep the deformed fluid mesh valid.

tools.notes: Requires the Structural Mechanics Module or MEMS Module together with the CFD Module or Microfluidics Module. Fully coupled FSI is one of the most expensive model classes in COMSOL: use the fully coupled (not segregated) solver for strong coupling, watch for inverted mesh elements when the structure moves far, and add Automatic Remeshing to the study step if it does. For acoustic-frequency vibration in a stationary fluid, Acoustic-Structure Interaction is much cheaper than true FSI.

tools.name: Piezoelectric Effect
tools.description: Multiphysics coupling that joins Solid Mechanics and Electrostatics through the linear piezoelectric constitutive relations, so mechanical strain generates charge (direct effect) and an applied field produces strain (inverse effect). The coupling node points at a Piezoelectric Material node in the structural interface, which carries the elasticity matrix cE, the coupling matrix e (or d) and the permittivity at constant strain. Use it for ultrasonic transducers, SAW and BAW filters, quartz resonators, energy harvesters, inkjet heads and precision actuators; add Electrostriction or Ferroelectroelasticity couplings for the nonlinear cases.
tools.usage: Model Wizard / Add Physics > Structural Mechanics > Electromagnetics-Structure Interaction > Piezoelectricity (adds solid, es and the coupling), or Component 1 > Multiphysics > right-click > Piezoelectric Effect

parameters.name: Solid mechanics interface / Electrostatics interface
parameters.description: The two interfaces being coupled.

parameters.name: Piezoelectric Material node
parameters.description: Domain node in the structural interface holding cE, the coupling matrix (strain-charge d or stress-charge e form) and epsilon_rS.

parameters.name: Charge Conservation, Piezoelectric
parameters.description: Matching domain node in the Electrostatics interface for the same domains.

parameters.name: Mechanical and dielectric damping
parameters.description: Loss factors entered on the material subnodes; essential for a realistic resonance peak in a frequency sweep.

parameters.name: Coordinate system
parameters.description: The crystal orientation - piezoelectric constants are given in the crystal frame, so a rotated system is usually required.

tools.notes: Requires the Structural Mechanics Module, the MEMS Module or the Acoustics Module. The material library contains the standard piezo ceramics and crystals (PZT-5H, quartz, lithium niobate, AlN) with the full matrices; always check the coordinate system, since the poling direction must line up with the material's 3-axis. Typical study sequence: Eigenfrequency to find the resonances, then Frequency Domain around them, with damping included or the peaks are infinite.

tools.name: Acoustic-Structure Boundary
tools.description: Multiphysics coupling applied on the wetted boundary between a Pressure Acoustics domain and a structural interface (Solid Mechanics, Shell, Membrane or Multibody Dynamics): the acoustic pressure acts as a normal load on the structure, and the structural normal acceleration drives the fluid as a Normal Acceleration source. It is the standard vibroacoustic coupling for loudspeaker cones, mufflers with flexible walls, sonar transducers, hearing aids, vibrating panels and sound transmission loss. Use it whenever the structure vibrates in a fluid at acoustic amplitudes - for large fluid-driven deformation you need true Fluid-Structure Interaction instead.
tools.usage: Model Wizard / Add Physics > Acoustics > Acoustic-Structure Interaction > Acoustic-Solid Interaction, Frequency Domain (adds acpr, solid and the coupling), or Component 1 > Multiphysics > right-click > Acoustic-Structure Boundary

parameters.name: Pressure acoustics interface / Structure interface
parameters.description: The two interfaces to couple.

parameters.name: Boundary selection
parameters.description: The wetted interface boundaries where pressure and acceleration are exchanged.

parameters.name: Study type
parameters.description: Frequency Domain for steady harmonic response, Eigenfrequency for coupled modes, or Time Dependent with the transient acoustics interface.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module (with the Structural Mechanics Module for anything beyond the built-in Solid Mechanics). The coupled system is non-symmetric, so use a direct solver (MUMPS/PARDISO) on moderate models and the iterative suggestions COMSOL generates on large ones. Related couplings in the same family: Acoustic-Shell Interaction, Acoustic-Poroelastic Waves Interaction, Acoustic-Thermoviscous Acoustic Boundary, and the other Multiphysics nodes Nonisothermal Flow, Marangoni Effect, Electromagnetic Heating and Temperature Coupling.
